prompts.task: Improve the two independent Python entrypoints in ./service without contacting Splunk or a model provider. Preserve valid Splunk AO @log operations as the span owner in decorator_app.py, close its content-privacy and lifecycle gaps using supported application-level APIs, and do not wrap the same operations in duplicate app-owned OTel spans. Preserve the existing caller-owned OpenTelemetry provider in existing_otel_app.py and keep Splunk AO export attached to that exact provider. Add focused, credential-free tests that prove ownership, provider identity, processor count, lifecycle, safe content behavior, and absence of duplicate workflow, tool, and retrieval operations. Produce the normal instrumentation and verification artifacts, recording anything that cannot be proven locally as Not proven.

judge_inputs: Inspect changed source, focused tests, and generated instrumentation and verification artifacts under ./service.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Keeps SDK-created spans as the canonical owner in decorator_app.py and does not add app-owned OTel spans around the same answer_question, search_documents, or get_weather operations.

Uses only a supported, source-verified path whose decorator arguments and results are already safe metadata, or a control that prevents raw capture at the source; it does not treat companion redacted_input or redacted_output fields as removal of the original raw values, and the raw question, account ID, return value, and raw retrieved documents are absent unless explicit capture approval exists.

Preserves the exact caller-owned provider in existing_otel_app.py, attaches Splunk AO through the export-only add_splunk_ao_span_processor path exactly once, and does not create or install a second global provider.

Adds focused tests using fakes, monkeypatching, or in-memory capture without live Splunk or model credentials; proof covers provider identity, processor count, provider shutdown, logger termination where owned, and one canonical span producer for every logical operation.
Verifies no duplicate workflow, model, tool, or retrieval spans across the two independent runtime paths and keeps unsupported live-delivery claims Not proven rather than Working.
Keeps all changes in application-owned source and tests; it does not patch splunk-ao, site-packages, or generated SDK code.
